articles.title_zh: 你就不能爱所有人吗？
articles.content: “Love one another.” This is one of the undeniable imperatives of Christianity. God is love (1 John 4:8, 16). We must love one another (1 John 4:11). By this love all men know that we are Christ’s disciples (John 13:35). Love fulfills the law (Romans 13:10). So why not just love one another? Why build walls, make distinctions, establish boundaries, and draw lines? Why confront sins? Why not welcome all equally? Can ’ t you just love everyone? The impulse and the argument “just to love everyone” is superficially attractive, even apparently compelling. However, the argument uses Bible language the way Satan does — selectively and deceptively. When tempting Christ, the devil selectively quoted Scripture but twisted the whole sense (cf. Matthew 4:5–7; Psalm 91:11–12). It is possible to use Bible language while ignoring the context, imposing a different meaning on the words and drawing false conclusions based on faulty assumptions. This regularly happens with the meaning of love . Does it really matter? Yes . Churches are disrupted and even destroyed by the confusion created by such shallow reading and reasoning. The language of love is thoroughly scriptural, but we need to handle our Bibles carefully. We need to understand the true definition and the proper direction and order of love. Love Defined and Established Think of love’s definition and foundation. Love does not appear in a vacuum, a sort of glowing, amorphous cloud of feeling which we can press into any mold. Rather, God defines it carefully. God’s love sets the standard for our love: In this the love of God was made manifest among us, that God sent his only Son into the world, so that we might live through him. In this is love, not that we have loved God but that he loved us and sent his Son to be the propitiation for our sins. Beloved, if God so loved us, we also ought to love one another. (1 John 4:9–11) God’s love, which we reflect and replicate by the Spirit’s power, is not a generic niceness but a determined act of the divine will, directed toward the utterly unlovely. It does not at all diminish or dilute the reality of sin. It faces sin’s pollution, punishment, and power head-on, fully honoring divine justice as well as divine mercy. It is love manifested in sacrifice, love determined to do heavenly good to its object, to make the unlovely lovely through whatever righteous means necessary. Christian people show a similar Godlike and Christlike love toward one another. Anticipating his sacrifice, our Lord says, A new commandment I give to you, that you love one another: just as I have loved you, you also are to love one another. By this all people will know that you are my disciples, if you have love for one another. (John 13:34) Christlike love for other believers is a mark of a true disciple. Because God in Christ sets the standard for what love looks like, we cannot collapse Christian love into mere sentimentality, a kind of anodyne sweetness that overlooks or dismisses sin and downplays righteousness. Love Directed and Ordered Think also of love’s direction and order. Our love for our brothers demonstrates our love for God himself (1 John 4:20–21). Our Lord goes to the cross for his beloved people out of love to his Father. The structure of the greatest commandment reveals both direction and order: First , love the Lord your God entirely, and second , love your neighbor as yourself (Matthew 22:37–40; Mark 12:29–31). While not denying a proper love of affinity, Christ calls us to a crowning love of supremacy: We are to love Christ more than father or mother, son or daughter (Matthew 10:37). Love for our nearest and dearest might even be considered hatred in comparison to the love that we have for him (Luke 14:26)! We must not, then, think of love first in its horizontal dimension toward men. Love must first be directed vertically toward God, in response to his love to us, before it spills over horizontally toward others. “Love” toward men at the expense of love t

articles.title_zh: 任务对儿童来说是否太昂贵？
articles.content: Are my children also called to this ? As a mama missionary, I wonder about our fitness for the task when our family of eight clogs airport security and labors in language study and ministry like a well-meaning circus. Will my kids catch a deadly virus from the airport carpet? Will beans be lunch every day ? How can we possibly replace years spent with grandparents and a vibrant children’s church? Will they become healthy adults when this calling cuts not only us but them? Are the unreached regions of the Joshua Project map reserved for singles? Our family’s plane-ticket prices alone might argue that case. Does the church only send the strong? In the world’s economy, our crew is inefficient and slow to get the job done. Risk Worth Reward The missionary call may cost our precious children extra bouts of food poisoning, power outages, awkward cultural moments, and loneliness. It may even, like Perpetua Broten and Ezra, Violet, and Calvin Pals , require their lives. When Jesus called his followers, he asked for painful, costly sacrifice. He reminded them that though foxes and birds return each day to their burrows and nests, he had no place to lay his head (Matthew 8:20). He called his disciples to take no change of clothes or spare coin for their ministry (Matthew 10:9–10). And yet he said, “There is no one who has left house or brothers or sisters or mother or father or children or lands, for my sake and for the gospel, who will not receive a hundredfold” both now and in eternity (Mark 10:29–30). God’s economy is not man’s. Jesus calls kids to go with moms and dads to serve the nations because God’s kingdom advancement is for families too, and the risk is worth its reward. The forward momentum of God’s kingdom does not exclude our children. The garden mandate to be fruitful and multiply now expands spiritually, and we take our kids along. We aren’t disqualified from overseas ministry if we’re changing diapers on the hour. God is the author of life and the genius behind the family design. Our dominion over the earth as image-bearers includes those in our care, even if they look too small to slay dragons. The risks of going with kids in tow are many; only the rewards of trust and obedience eclipse their reality. If we pursued mere adventure or greater cultural appreciation, we would be the “most to be pitied” (1 Corinthians 15:19). But if God calls us to glory in Christ in dungeon-like places, teaching our children to cup their hands around their mouths and cry to prisoners, “Come out!” then we offer them diamond-quality joy (Isaiah 49:9, 61:1). We weep with our kids over the cost they see and feel in their own lives, helping them gather the broken pieces of their hearts to hand to Jesus, teaching them firsthand that Christ’s flesh and blood satisfy. Shepherding Your Flock Before my two oldest children were dunked in the cold mountain water of our village in baptism, they testified to God’s grace in their lives. God had shown them his best at their worst. I flinched inwardly as I heard them recall dangerous accidents and desperate emotions in our time overseas. But when it turned darkest, God shone brightest. If it were up to me, I would have taken an eraser to God’s plan of pain for them. If I had, I would also have unknowingly rubbed out his intimate deliverances. The pleasure of following God to the farthest reaches of the planet with your kids is finding that God is there too. All that said, our family just moved ministry locations overseas due to prolonged isolation and our kids’ growing need for friends and community. Missions is a family affair and worth the risk, while at the same time, God does not depend on our presence in a place to accomplish his purposes, and he cares specifically for our kids. Our kids’ particular needs are not at odds with our calling but can direct our feet and make us wise shepherds of our flock. God is not biting his nails on the sidelines of our missionary service, hoping we’ll perform well enou
articles.content_zh:
我的孩子也被叫来了吗? 作为一位母亲传教士,我想知道我们是否适合完成这项任务,当我们这个8个堵塞的机场保安和劳工家庭在语言学习和像一个善意的马戏团一样的部委工作时。 我的孩子会从机场地毯上感染致命病毒吗? 每天吃豆子吃午饭吗? 我们怎样才能取代在祖父母和充满活力的儿童教堂度过的岁月?

他们会不会成为健康的成年人 当这个呼吁不仅削减我们,而且削减他们? 约书亚计划图中未进入的地区是否为单人保留? 我们家族的飞机票价本身就可能证明这一点。 教会只派强者吗? 在世界经济中,我们的船员效率低下,完成任务的速度缓慢。

值得回报的风险 传教士的召唤可能使我们珍贵的孩子们额外损失食物中毒、断电、尴尬的文化时刻和孤独。 它甚至可能像Perpetua Broten和Ezra、Violet和Calvin Pals一样需要他们的生命。 当耶稣召唤他的追随者时,他要求痛苦,昂贵的牺牲.

他提醒他们,虽然狐狸和鸟儿每天返回他们的洞穴和巢穴,但他没有地方安顿头颅(Matthew 8:20). 他叫门徒们不要为他们的部会换衣服或多余的硬币(Matthew 10:9-10).

然而,他却说,“没有人离开过家,也没有人离开过兄弟姐妹,也没有人离开过母亲、孩子或土地,为了我和福音,现在和永远都得不到一百倍”(Mark 10:29-30)。 上帝的经济不是人类的经济。

因为上帝的王国进步也是为了家庭, 上帝王国的前进势头并不排除我们的孩子。 花园的任务富有成果,倍增,现在精神上有所扩展,我们带着我们的孩子一起走.

如果我们换尿布, 上帝是生命的作者,也是家庭设计背后的天才. 我们作为形象持有者对地球的统治权包括那些受我们照顾的人,即使他们看起来太小,不能杀死龙。 和孩子一起被拖走的风险是很多的;只有信任和服从的回报掩盖了他们的现实。

如果我们仅仅追求冒险或更大的文化欣赏,我们将“最可怜”(科林斯15:19)。 但是,如果上帝在类似地牢的地方召唤我们在基督中荣耀,教我们的孩子用手握住嘴,向囚犯喊叫,“出来吧!”那么我们给他们提供钻石质量的快乐(以赛亚49:9,61:1)。

我们和孩子们一起为他们自己生活中所看到和感受到的代价而哭泣,帮助他们收集心碎的碎片交给耶稣,并亲身教他们基督的血肉满足。 在我两个年长的孩子 被浸在村里的寒冷山水里之前 他们证明了上帝的恩惠

上帝在他们最坏的时候 给他们展示了他最好的一面 当我听到他们回想起我们海外时代的危险事故和绝望情绪时,我内向退缩。 但当它变得最黑暗时,上帝会闪耀 如果由我决定的话,我本来会用一个抹除器去完成上帝给他们的痛苦计划。 如果我有的话,我也会不知不觉地 抹去他的亲切奉献。

和你们的孩子一起跟随上帝到达地球最远的地方的乐趣 就是发现上帝也在那里 我们的家人因为长期孤立和孩子对朋友和社区的日益需求,刚刚将部属迁往海外。

使命是一种家庭事务,值得冒风险,与此同时,上帝并不依赖我们的存在来实现他的目的,他特别关心我们的孩子. 我们的孩子的特殊需求与我们的召唤并不矛盾,

articles.title: To Sustain Inner-City Church Plants, Adopt a Missionary Model
articles.summary: To plant churches in these spaces, we need to think like missionaries.
articles.summary_zh: 要在这些地方建造教堂，我们需要像传教士一样思考。
articles.title_zh: 为了维持内城教会植物，采用传教士模式
articles.content: In a conversation at church one Sunday, a pastor told a friend of mine, “Your friend should quit trying to plant churches in the inner city. It doesn’t happen because it can’t happen.” I was visiting this friend just before COVID-19 hit, speaking at a separate church about our ministry, New England Urban Church Planting. Our organization was new, and my sinful inclination was to think, Oh, you just wait and see! My friend was equally defensive. Yet this pastor was onto something: It rarely happens, and it is indeed hard. Why is church planting in our nation’s neglected inner cities so rare? Why are underserved urban communities overlooked by gospel-preaching churches? Stakeholders in our ministry have discussed these questions since 2009, leading to the organization’s founding in 2020. We’ve learned a lot in these years of full-time work as we’re growing this network of inner-city planters. The work is hard for two key reasons. Yet it’s possible. And it’s crucial. Christ has commanded us to make disciples of all nations (Matt. 28:19)—this includes in our own nation’s inner cities. To plant churches in these spaces, we need to think like missionaries. Problem Unless you grew up in the inner city, serving there is a cross-cultural experience. This is the first reason church planting hard. Ruby Payne asks her readers if they can survive in poverty: Do you know how to keep your clothes from being stolen from a laundromat? Do you know how to move in half a day? Do you know how to keep your car from getting repossessed if you fall behind on payments? Discipling men and women in the inner city can be exasperating when they have a new burner phone frequently. Inner-city pastors need to know how to preach and how to administer Narcan. And behind all that is the sound of gunshots, fights, loud TVs, and the quiet exit of well-meaning suburban Christians who came to help but didn’t last long. Christ has commanded us to make disciples of all nations—this includes in our own nation’s inner cities. Evangelicalism often feels like it’s married to only one culture: suburbia. Postwar Americans migrated from our cities to set up homes and churches in the suburbs. In 1940, 15 percent of Americans lived in the suburbs. By 2000, that number was 50 percent. Evangelicals were a disproportionately high percentage of those who made the move. As this happened, Brian Miller argues , the values of suburbia melded with and shaped the values of evangelicalism. Churches in impoverished neighborhoods are rarely financially self-sustaining—the second challenge. Even if a pastor disciples his church toward generosity, being generous with a poverty-level income won’t pay the bills. So pastors who serve in these places get beaten down by serving a needy congregation while holding two other jobs “on the side.” It’s unsustainable. We don’t believe the answer for inner-city pastors should be a bi- or trivocational life. Solution The solution to these two challenges is within reach: the model of a supported foreign missionary. Since the late 18th century, the church has been training and sustaining men and women for gospel work in unfamiliar places, where they cannot expect the financial support of locals. This training-and-supporting model should be applied to inner-city church planting. The change we need has four aspects. The first is a change of heart. We need gospel-saturated hearts that understand that all people are impoverished by sin. Those living in a homeless encampment share the same fundamental condition as the wealthy suburbanite. Filled with gospel grace, we can move toward the poor because we’re more alike at heart than we are different. Our hearts must be shaped by the reality of Christ’s initiative to leave the riches of heaven for us, to become poor for us, that we might become rich (2 Cor. 8:9). Second, we need to believe that God’s heart is particularly inclined toward the overlooked (Ps. 72:12–14) and toward those generous toward them (Prov. 14:

articles.title: Report Cards on Your Actions Won’t Fix Your Heart
articles.summary: From GLP-1s to political reposts to mindfulness streaks, we’re all keeping score. Jesus says you can’t know who you are until you look at your heart.
articles.summary_zh: 从GLP-1到政治转发，再到正念条纹，我们都在记分。耶稣说，除非你看看自己的内心，否则你无法知道自己是谁。
articles.title_zh: 关于您行动的报告卡片无法修复您的心脏
articles.content: Who am I? All cultures, human philosophies, and religious systems try to answer this question in a way that leads to a meaningful life. We want to find in them a path that allows us to say, “Who am I? I’m a good person. I’m someone who is living a good and right life.” What paths toward goodness and righteousness are being offered today? They’re as vast and varied as ever. One popular path is to optimize your life via medical improvements, ranging from plastic surgery to GLP-1s. The more you can “ humanmaxx ” your body to look healthier and be stronger, the more likely you’ll be considered an ideal human being—a good person to hire, to be friends with, to date or marry. Political engagement is another common path. Your goodness is determined by how connected you are to particular political movements. You can feel like you’re a good person when you make sure you quickly like and repost all Zohran Mamdani’s videos. Or alternatively, you’ll be affirmed as a good person by how aggressively you go after or insult people who like Mamdani. Paths our culture offers to the good life are often combined. Your sense of how good a person you are is measured by a mixture of how long you’ve engaged in therapy, how many hours you volunteer at your children’s school, and how long your streak is on your mindfulness app. Tara Isabella Burton, in her book Strange Rites: New Religions for a Godless World , argues that people have formed their own religious systems by drawing from various religions and philosophies. People have become “creators of their own bespoke religions, mixing and matching spiritual and aesthetic and experiential and philosophical traditions.” We’re doing a DIY project, grabbing and piecing together whatever’s around us, hoping we can come up with something to help us in our journey. So, what path does Christianity offer to assure us we’re living a good and righteous life? Keeping Score The Christian approach is to address what the Bible calls the heart. The heart is the Bible’s shorthand term for describing the part of you that drives and motivates you, what dictates your thoughts and emotions. Christianity starts with the heart because this is the only real way by which you can determine who you are and what needs to change. We see the contrast between the religious and cultural approach and the Christian approach in Jesus’s interaction with the Pharisees in Matthew 15:1–20. The Pharisees confront Jesus to ask him why his disciples don’t wash their hands before eating. Handwashing before meals was one of the many religious rules the Pharisees had developed, practiced, and called others to practice. For the Pharisees, the best answer to the question “Who am I?” was based on how well they followed their set standards. If a person kept the standard and had a life that could be observed to follow all the rules, then that person could definitively say to themselves and those around them, “I’m a good person who is living a good and right life.” Jesus’s story about the Pharisee in Luke 18:9–14 is another example. The Pharisee intently notes in his prayer how he, unlike the tax collector praying next to him, fasts twice a week and always gives the full tithe. Jesus describes the Pharisees in Matthew 6 as people who make sure their regular prayers can be seen and affirmed by all. The Pharisees weren’t alone in this approach. Greco-Roman religion had its own rules and standards to follow. Its gods demanded rituals, sacrifices, and festivals to appease and honor them. Performed rightly, they’d result in people securing the blessing they needed from the gods, thus assuring them their lives were good and righteous. Jesus, however, reframes the Pharisees’ questioning by showing that their approach doesn’t go far enough. Right living and human flourishing demands more than one’s outward actions. It requires harder interior examination. And that means looking at the heart. Jesus says, “What comes out of the mouth proceeds from the heart” (

我是谁? 所有文化,人类哲学,宗教体系都试图以导致有意义的生活的方式来回答这个问题. 我们想在他们中间找到一条道路,使我们能够说:“我是谁? 我是个好人。 我是一个过着良好和正确生活的人。 今天为善良和正义提供了哪些途径? 他们和以往一样,

一个通俗的途径是通过医疗改进来优化你的生活,从整形手术到GLP-1. 你越能"人类马克思"你的身体看起来越健康,越强壮,你就越有可能被认为是理想的人——一个能雇佣、成为朋友、约会或结婚的好人。 政治参与是另一条共同道路。

你的善良取决于你和特定政治运动的关系 也觉得自己是个好人, 或以你对马姆达尼的追求或侮辱来证明你是一个好人。 我们的文化为美好生活提供的道路常常是结合在一起的。

你对一个人有多好的感觉,是通过你从事治疗的时间、你在学校志愿工作多少小时、以及你的心智应用上多久来衡量的。

Tara Isabella Burton在她所著"陌生的Rites:新宗教为无神的世界"一书中认为,人们通过从各种宗教和哲学中汲取来形成自己的宗教体系.

人们已经成为“他们自己所讲的宗教的创造者,混合和配合精神和美学以及体验和哲学传统。” 我们正在进行一个DIY计划, 抓取和整理我们周围的东西, 希望我们能想出一些东西来帮助我们的旅程。 基督教给我们提供了什么途径来保证我们过着美好和正义的生活?

记分 基督教的方法是解决"圣经"所说的"心". 心灵是圣经的简称,用来描述你推动和激励你,决定你思想和情绪的部分。 基督教以心为起点,因为这是你决定自己是谁和需要改变的惟一真正方法.

在耶稣与法利赛人的互动中, 法利赛人面对耶稣, 餐前洗手是法利赛人制定,练习的众多宗教规则之一,并号召其他人去练习.

对法利赛人来说,“我是谁?” 问题的最佳答案在于他们遵守既定标准的情况。

如果一个人能遵守标准,并过着可以遵守所有规则的生活,那么这个人可以肯定地对自己和周围的人说,“我是个好人,正在过上良好和正确的生活。” 耶稣在卢克18:9–14中讲述了法利赛人的故事是另一个例子.

法利赛人在祷告中故意记下他如何与旁边的收税者不同的是,他每周斋戒两次并总是给满分之一. 耶稣在"马太福音"6中将法利赛人描述为确保他们的定期祷告能被所有人都看到和肯定的人. 法利赛人并不孤单。 格雷科-罗马宗教有自己的规则和标准可以遵循。

它的神要求举行仪式,祭祀,并举行节日来安抚和尊崇他们. 让他们得到神赐予的祝福, 但耶稣重新定义了法利赛人的质疑,

正确的生活和人类的繁荣需要不止一种外向行动。 这需要更严格的内部检查。 并谓观心相. 耶稣说,“从口中出出的东西从心脏中得来。”

articles.title_zh: 邪恶如何运作
articles.content: Audio Transcript What does evil look like? And sound like? And feel like? Is evil like a horror film set in a haunted forest in a remote cabin at night with floorboards creaking under uninvited footsteps? Or is evil the most scandalous murder trial in the headlines? Is evil more quiet, like in white-collar crimes and embezzlement? Or is it a bloody civil war? There are many forms evil can take. But at its core, how evil works is more essential than all those things I just described. Today on Ask Pastor John: how evil works. This week in our Bible reading, we come upon a trio of texts that collectively reveal to us Satan’s multifront assault — how he works in this world. He is a spiritual deceiver of minds, he is a prosecuting accuser in the heavenly courtroom, and he is a behind-the-scenes influence in human rebellion. He seems to work in a lot of different ways. In John 8 we see him as a liar and murderer. In 2 Peter 2–3 we see him as the deceiver and destroyer. And in Job 4–6 we see him as the provocateur and accuser. Those roles help reveal his work to us in the world. And as we rehearse these roles in our Bible reading this week, we have this email from an anonymous young man. “Pastor John, when I think about spiritual warfare, I often first think about physical things like illness and addiction and even demonic possession. But I wonder if I am missing a larger picture. How much influence does Satan have in this world, and how does he use it? How much of his power is physical? How much of it is unseen? And where do you see him most at work in our modern culture? Is it in obvious sins? Or in subtler ways to keep people from the gospel? How can I see his work without getting preoccupied with him?” A great question with clear purpose. Here’s how Pastor John answered this very question from a young man named Josh in 2018. How Satan Works The word Satan is a transliteration of the Hebrew Satan (śāṭān) and basically means “opponent” or “adversary.” The Greek translation of the Hebrew Old Testament always translates Satan with diabolos in Greek, which means “devil”; we always translate diabolos in English, in the New Testament, “devil.” And diabolos puts a more specific focus on the meaning of the opponent or adversary because diabolos basically means “slander” or “accuse.” It’s used not only to refer to the devil; several times in the Pastoral Epistles of Paul, it’s used to refer to people who are slandering others, speaking evil of them, being false about them. So, even though this supernatural being, this fallen angel and archenemy of God, has a remarkable power in the material or physical realm — he can make people sick, he can throw them in prison, he can even kill them — nevertheless, his main way of opposing God and destroying God’s people is not in the physical or material realm but in the mental or intellectual or moral realm. In other words, the best way to think about his power is not in terms of physical strength but moral deception. Let me try to illustrate this from the Bible. Here’s the passage that piles up more designations of Satan than any other passage in the Bible. If you need one or two verses to put the identity and work of Satan before you, it would be Revelation 12:9–10. Here it says, “And the great dragon was thrown down, that ancient serpent.” And remember what the Bible said in Genesis 3:1 about him. He’s subtler than every beast. So, it’s his subtlety that’s being focused on in his serpent-like reality. “[He] is called the devil [diabolos: slanderer, liar, cheat] and Satan [adversary], the deceiver of the whole world” (Revelation 12:9). I don’t think you can say anything more sweeping or more basic than Revelation 12:9–10. “The accuser of our brothers has been thrown down, who accuses them day and night before our God” (Revelation 12:10). So, at the center of Satan’s purpose is to deceive on earth and to accuse in heaven. If he can deceive you about God and Christ, you will perish. If he can successfu

articles.summary_zh: 将讲道视为一门科学有助于我们理解，我们可以运用一些工具来更好地完成工作。把它看作一门艺术提醒我们，这件作品需要我们关注圣经宣讲的美丽。帮助初学者和经验丰富的传教士：大卫·杰克曼（ David Jackman ）的《从文本到教学》（ From Text to Teaching ）一文首先出现在9Marks上。
articles.title_zh: 初学者和经验丰富的传教士的帮助：大卫·杰克曼从文本到教学的回顾
articles.content: Abstract: Jeremy Meeks reviews David Jackman’s From Text to Teaching: A Guide to Preparing Bible Talks and commends it as a helpful resource for anyone who preaches or teaches the Bible in any context. This brief book offers discussions of the art and science of preaching and the process of preparation, and it provides an inside look at Jackman’s own preparation to preach 1 Corinthians 1–4. The final chapters offer checklists that will be practically useful for preachers, and the appendix contains the author’s own template for preparing a Bible talk. Both beginners and seasoned preachers and teachers will benefit from this book. David Jackman, From Text to Teaching: A Guide to Preparing Bible Talks . Matthias Media, 2021. 92 pp. Even seasoned preacher needs to go back to basics sometimes and be refreshed. Similarly, guys starting out need instruction—someone to teach them how to go about the craft. Often the most helpful teachers are those who have lots of experience. What is even better is if such a preacher has also spent substantial time training others to preach. Ideally, that preacher/trainer has such command of the material that he is able to distill his insights and counsel into a tight, readable book. We have been given such a gift in David Jackman’s little volume From Text to Teaching . In just 92 pages, Jackman provides a lifetime of wisdom for the beginner and the seasoned preacher alike. As he explains in the introduction, he is addressing (as evidenced in the title) the skill of Bible teaching more generally and not solely preaching. This might turn away preachers who don’t consider themselves to be giving “Bible talks,” but that would be the preacher’s loss. The weight of what we get to do every time we open the Bible and teach from it in any context is rightly esteemed by Jackman. The Art and Science of Preaching The book begins by discussing the “Art and Science of Preaching.” Both aspects of preaching—art and science—must be held onto if we are to do it well. Seeing preaching as a science helps us understand that there are tools we can apply to do the work better. Seeing it as an art reminds us that the work requires us to pay attention to the beauty of Bible proclamation. Preaching is more than using the Bible to communicate. Rather, our task is to preach what the text says, that is, giving the meaning of what it says, in context, for the people sitting in front of us. Jackman’s convictions will be new to some, common to others, but beneficial to all. The Process of Preparation A substantial chapter is dedicated to the “Process of Preparation”. Here Jackman helps the Bible preacher/teacher think through how to put a message together. As a preacher who trains other preachers, I’m constantly asked how I do this on a weekly basis, and I enjoy hearing how others do it as well. Jackman has sage advice. He reminds us that we should always be praying (an obvious but seriously neglected aspect of preparation). He is also clear that we should use the time we have strategically. We never have as much time as we would like, and we often think we need more time than we do. The fact is that preachers often waste a lot of time because they are not strategic. Jackman recommends setting aside a few blocks of time in the week (four sessions that are each two to three hours). What is vital is that the preacher figures out what works well for him and plans his schedule accordingly. Jackman then gives helpful advice on how to go about studying and writing out the sermon inside those blocks of time, and this advice is helpful for those at all levels of proficiency. Invited into the Author’s Study The next three chapters (3–5) of the book are pure gold. In essence, Jackman invites us into his study to listen in as he walks through his process of preparing messages on 1 Corinthians 1–4. Here we get insights into how his suggested process works in actual texts. This is something many books on preaching neglect to do, leaving the rea

摘要:杰里米·米克(Jeremy Meeks)评论了大卫·杰克曼的"从文字到教学:准备圣经谈话的指南",并称赞它是任何背景中宣扬或教授圣经的人的有用资源. 这本简短的书提供了对布道的艺术和科学以及准备过程的讨论,它提供了杰克曼自己为布道1科林斯1–4的准备的内观.

最后的章节提供了对传道者实际上有用的核对表,附录中包含了作者自己准备圣经演讲的模板. 初学者和老练的传道人和教师都将受益于这本书。 David Jackman,《从文字到教学:准备圣经会谈指南》,Matthias Media,2021年。

甚至老练的传教士有时也需要回到基础,被刷新. 类似地,开始的人需要教书,有人教他们如何操作这款工艺。 最有帮助的教师往往是经验丰富的教师。 更好的是,如果这种传道者也花大量时间训练其他人传道。

理想的情况是,传教士/教官对材料有如此高的指挥力,他能够将自己的见解和咨询意见提炼成一本紧凑可读的书。 在大卫·杰克曼的"从文字到教学"一书中,我们得到了这样的礼物。 在92页里,杰克曼为初学者和老练的传道者提供了一生的智慧.

正如他在导言中所解释的,他正在讨论(如标题所证明的)《圣经》教学的技巧更普遍,而不仅仅是传道。 这可能会让那些不认为自己在进行“圣经会谈”的传道者退后,

每当我们打开圣经并在任何背景中从中教导时,我们所能做的事情的分量都得到了杰克曼的正确尊重. 该书首先讨论了“影响艺术与科学”。 如果我们要做得好,就必须坚持艺术和科学两个方面的传道。

将传道视为一种科学,有助于我们理解,我们可以应用一些工具来更好地开展工作。 把它看作是一门艺术,提醒我们,这部作品需要我们关注"圣经"宣言的美. 意义不仅仅是用"圣经"来沟通.

相反,我们的任务是宣扬案文所说的话,即在背景上赋予案文所述的含义,供坐在我们前面的人民使用。 杰克曼的信念对一些人来说是新的,对另一些人来说是共同的,但对所有人都有好处。 1. 编写过程

在这里,杰克曼帮助"圣经"的传道人/老师思考如何将一个信息集中起来. 作为一名培养其他传教士的传教士, 我经常问每周我怎么做, 杰克曼有圣人的建议 他提醒我们,我们应当永远祈祷(准备工作中一个明显但被严重忽略的方面)。

他还明确指出,我们应该从战略角度利用我们的时间。 我们从来没有像我们想要的那样多的时间,我们常常认为我们需要比我们多的时间。 事实是道教经常会因为不具有战略意义而浪费大量时间. 杰克曼建议在一周内留出几块时间(每两到三小时四会).

重要的是,传道者要知道什么对他很有效,并据此规划他的时间安排。 杰克曼随后就如何研究并写出这些时间段内的布道给出了有益的建议,而这个建议对于所有水平的熟练程度的人都是有帮助的. 书中接下来的三章(3–5)是纯金.

基本上,杰克曼邀请我们进入他的书房 在他行走的过程中聆听 他准备了科林斯1 -4的信息。 在这里,我们深入了解他建议的进程如何在实际文本中发挥作用。 这是很多书 关于布道 忽略做,留下的灵性

articles.content: According to the Belgic Confession , God reveals himself to us in two “books”: the book of nature (God’s world) and the book of Scripture (God’s written Word). The primary way God reveals himself in the book of Scripture is by proclaiming his name. In this first of two paired lectures from TGC25, Scott Swain considers several of the names whereby God reveals himself in the Bible. Contemplating God’s names provides a deeper understanding of his being and attributes and a firmer foundation for our faith and hope. It also helps us better appreciate the ways God reveals himself to us in Jesus Christ. articles.title: ‘I Play Rocky’ Finds New Inspiration in an Old Story
articles.summary: ‘I Play Rocky’ is the latest pop-culture celebration of storytelling as agency: telling your story in just the way you want it to be told.
articles.summary_zh: “I Play Rocky”是将讲故事作为代理的最新流行文化庆祝活动：以您希望的方式讲述您的故事。
articles.title_zh: 《我扮演洛基》在古老的故事中寻找新的灵感
articles.content: Rocky debuted in theaters 50 years ago, in 1976—a bicentennial-year release that underscored the movie’s profound American spirit. Immediately a blockbuster and critical darling (the highest-grossing movie of 1976 and winner of the Best Picture Oscar), it has since become a pantheon film in American cinema. Rocky ’s Philadelphia setting and underdog, rags-to-riches story captured a hardscrabble American optimism, something that gave needed inspiration in the mid-1970s and resonates still today. Now in 2026—America’s semiquincentennial— Rocky is getting a theatrical rerelease. And a new movie, I Play Rocky (out today in select theaters) is telling the story of the iconic movie’s development, which is an underdog epic of its own. The movie, directed by Peter Farrelly ( Green Book ) and starring Anthony Ippolito in a breakout turn as Sylvester Stallone, is a refreshingly feel-good crowd pleaser. It’s the sort of well-made, intelligent, but also inspiring movie for grown-ups that feels like a dying breed in Hollywood. Movies About Moviemaking I Play Rocky (rated PG-13 for language) follows a well-worn template of a movie about the making of a classic movie. Saving Mr. Banks (2013) was about Walt Disney and the making of Mary Poppins . Hitchcock (2012) was about Alfred Hitchcock and the making of Psycho . Last year’s Nouvelle Vague was about Jean-Luc Godard and the making of Breathless . I Play Rocky is about Stallone and the making of Rocky . Hollywood loves making movies about itself: stories about storytelling, movies about moviemaking, actors playing actors. Hollywood loves making movies about itself: stories about storytelling, movies about moviemaking, actors playing actors. Self-reflexive inspiration goes back more than a century in cinema, perhaps starting with Dziga Vertov’s Man with a Movie Camera (1929). The 1950s produced classics like Sunset Boulevard (1950) and Singin’ in the Rain (1952), but the trend really picked up in the postmodern era in the 1960s and beyond: 8 ½ (1963), Day for Night (1973), Mulholland Drive (2001), Adaptation (2002), The Artist (2011), and Once Upon a Time . . . in Hollywood (2019). The list is long. A hallmark of postmodernity is a metaposture of knowing awareness—storytellers who know they’re storytellers and want the audience to know that they know. As postmodernism has given way to metamodernism , the trend of “movies about moviemaking” has continued, but in a slightly different register. These sorts of films are no longer merely metaexercises in self-awareness. The cerebral, cynical detachment of “films about filmmaking” like Barton Fink (1991), Ed Wood (1994), or even Who Framed Roger Rabbit (1988) has given way to metamodern expressions that blend cynicism and sincerity, self-awareness with earnest escapism. Steven Spielberg’s The Fabelmans (2022) is a recent example of a movie in this vein, and I Play Rocky has a similar feel. Even as it lifts the veil on the Hollywood myth factory and mines many laughs out of the fundamentally profit-seeking, money-centric nature of the movie business, it’s full of heart and soul. It has a joyful, hopeful, sincere, perhaps idealistic spirit (“I’d rather be an optimist and be wrong, than a pessimist and be right,” one character says). Refreshing Celebration of Marriage I also like how I Play Rocky celebrates the empowering beauty of marriage. The film opens with Stallone as a broke actor in New York, sometimes sleeping on the streets and at one point accepting a role in an X-rated adult film just to earn some desperately needed money (a dark part of Stallone’s past that the film plays for awkward laughs). He’s a lost soul with bleak prospects. But then he meets Sasha (AnnaSophia Robb), with whom he works at a movie theater. They get married and move to Los Angeles, and things start to turn around for him. As a husband and soon a father, Stallone feels more urgency to provide. articles.title: How the Lord’s Supper Fuels Spiritual Growth
articles.summary: Calvin shows us that the Lord’s Supper is fuel for spiritual growth, so we should come to the table expectantly every time.
articles.summary_zh: 加尔文向我们表明，主的晚餐是灵性成长的燃料，所以我们每次都应该期待地来到餐桌前。
articles.title_zh: 主的晚餐如何促进灵性成长
articles.content: Recently, I (and my peers) have experienced a number of parishioners converting to Catholicism. As I’ve talked to these converts, they’ve consistently brought up the Lord’s Table. They find encouragement in identifying the bread and wine with Jesus’s body and blood. I’ve heard statements such as this: Pastor George, I like the idea that Jesus was talking about the Lord’s supper when he said, “Whoever feeds on my flesh and drinks my blood abides in me, and I in him” (John 6:56). My faith just feels more real if I’m literally bringing Jesus into my body on a daily basis. While this phenomenon seems to be happening with greater frequency, it’s not totally new. Years ago, I served alongside a man at an ordination service for another pastor in our city. I hadn’t met this man before; I only knew he had until recently been a professor at a Reformed and evangelical seminary. This man preached a solid message on Jesus’s call for ministers of the gospel, and I thanked him for it. Then, the next day, I saw him being interviewed on TV. I tuned in just as he explained, I needed more realism than my tradition provided, so during lunch I would walk down to the local Roman Catholic parish and take the Eucharist. To unite literally with Jesus’s body and blood was more deeply satisfying to me than the “mystery of union with Christ” my church taught. So, I resigned my post at the seminary and went home to Rome. I could relate other conversations with those who have left the Reformed faith and joined the Roman Catholic, Orthodox, or Anglo-Catholic traditions. A similar theme runs through them all: the desire for a more transformational, sensory reality than what the Reformed view of the Lord’s supper provides. Is this critique valid? How would John Calvin respond to the critique that if you follow the Reformed view of the supper, you’re missing out on its power? Transformed at the Table Sometimes, in an effort to have biblically faithful theology, Reformed Christians speak only of what the communion elements are not . I’m painfully aware of my of shortcomings in this regard. This can inadvertently drive some believers to seek out a more “real” experience in other traditions. We can get caught up in debating the exact nature of the bread and wine and forget to ask the more pressing question: How should this meal change me today? Let’s look back at Calvin’s teachings on communion. When we do, we’ll recover a renewed vision for the table, one that sees it as a divine encounter that motivates a transformed life of profound gratitude and obedience. In short, Calvin shows us that the Lord’s supper is fuel for spiritual growth, so we should come to the table expectantly every time. In Calvin’s “ Short Treatise on the Lord’s Supper ,” he writes that the supper fuels the believer’s spiritual growth in at least three ways. 1. The supper assures us of our inheritance in Christ. Calvin teaches that Jesus uses his table to assure us of our inheritance. He doesn’t merely mean that the supper gives us a psychological boost. He means that assurance comes by means of a real union between Christ and the believer, and he means that our experience of this union is expedited by faithfully partaking in the covenant meal. Calvin shows us that the Lord’s supper is fuel for spiritual growth, so we should come to the table expectantly every time. In his commentary on Ephesians, Calvin writes , “Paul says that we are members of his [Christ’s] flesh and of his bones. Do we wonder then, that in the Lord’s Supper he holds out his body to be enjoyed by us, and to nourish us unto eternal life?” Calvin insists that by faith, Christians are made members of Jesus’s fleshly human body, so at communion, we experience all the benefits of spiritual union with him. Christ took on flesh so that in his ascended state, he might be a channel of righteousness to the believer, pouring into him all that Christ’s human life accomplished. 最近,我(和我的同龄人)经历了一些皈依天主教的教区人士. 当我和这些皈依者交谈时, 他们发现鼓励用耶稣的身体和血液来识别面包和葡萄酒。

我听到过这样的话:乔治牧师,我喜欢耶稣在谈论主的晚餐,他说:“谁吃我的肉喝我的血,谁在我体内,我就在他体内”(John 6:56)。 如果我每天把耶稣带入我的身体, 虽然这种现象似乎更频繁地发生,

多年前,我和一个男人一起 为我们市的另一位牧师服务 我之前从未见过这个人;我只知道他直到最近才成为一所改革后福音神学院的教授。 这个人在耶稣号召福音的大臣们时宣扬一个坚实的信息,我为此感谢他. 然后,第二天,我看到他接受电视采访。

正如他所解释的,我需要比传统更现实的, 所以在午餐期间,我会走进罗马天主教当地的教区, 并带上尤查里会。 比起教会教义的“与基督结合的谜团”, 于是我辞去神学院的职务,回到了罗马.

我可以和那些脱离改革后信仰并加入罗马天主教、东正教或天主教传统的人交谈。 一个类似的主题贯穿于所有这些方面:渴望一个比改革后对主的晚餐提供的看法更具有转型性、感官性的现实。 这种批评有道理吗?

约翰·卡尔文会如何回应这种批评:如果你遵循改革后的晚餐观, 有时候,为了实现圣经上忠实的神学,改革后的基督徒只谈论圣餐的内容。 我痛苦地意识到我在这方面的缺点。

这可能无意中驱使一些信徒在其他传统中寻求更“真实”的经验。 我们可以在辩论面包和葡萄酒的确切性质时陷入困境,并忘记提出更紧迫的问题: 今天这顿饭怎么能改变我? 让我们回顾加尔文关于圣餐的教义。

我们将会重新恢复对桌子的憧憬, 简言之,加尔文告诉我们,主的晚餐是精神成长的燃料,因此,我们每次都应该期待地来到餐桌旁。

他写道, 晚餐至少以三种方式促进信徒的精神成长。 1. 晚餐保证了我们在基督的遗产。 加尔文教耶稣用桌子保证我们的遗产 他不只是说晚餐会给我们心理上的刺激。

articles.title_zh: 救赎使你成为家庭的一部分：皈依的企业组成部分
articles.content: Abstract : Jonathan Leeman highlights the corporate component of conversion, pointing out that God not only reconciles us to himself through Christ but also to one another. While our (vertical) reconciliation to God is foundational and primary, our (horizontal) reconciliation to others is necessarily bound up with our salvation. Conversion makes us part of God’s people, and this corporate aspect of our salvation should compel us to join a local church. Editor’s Note: This article is taken from Church Matters, the 9Marks journal for pastors, in the issue titled Conversion . If your doctrine of conversion is missing the corporate element, it’s missing something essential. Jesus died for a people (see Mark 10:45). He saves us as individuals, and he saves us into a people. Salvation includes a family. If you’re not convinced, jump straight to these parallel statements from Peter: Once you were not a people, but now you are God’s people; once you had not received mercy, but now you have received mercy. (1 Pet. 2:10) If someone asks you how you became a Christian, you probably emphasize the second line in your testimony. You say something like, “I was living in sin apart from God. A friend shared the gospel with me. I recognized who God is and what Christ did in dying and rising again. Therefore, I repented and believed. Praise God, he forgave me and I received his mercy!” What a wonderful testimony. Don’t stop saying that! Widen Your Perspective But notice that Peter widens the aperture of the camera and tells us a little more about what happened in that same moment. In addition to moving from not mercy to mercy, we simultaneously moved from not a people to a people. That means our testimonies could include a little bit more. Like this: “I was living in sin apart from God, and I wanted nothing to do with God’s family, the church. A friend shared the gospel with me. I recognized who God is and what Christ did in dying and rising again. Therefore, I repented and believed. Praise God, he forgave me and I received his mercy! I also realized that—wow!—I was part of a family now, the church.” Do you see what I mean by the “corporate” component of conversion? We’re saved into the universal church. That’s not to say we should put the corporate element out front. One might think of N. T. Wright’s well-known line about justification being “not so much about soteriology as about ecclesiology; not so much about salvation as about the church . ” N.T. Wright, What Saint Paul Really Said (Eerdmans, 20 1 4), 1 1 9. This is a clear example, in Douglas Moo’s almost-as-well-known line, of backgrounding what the New Testament foregrounds, and foregrounding what the New Testament backgrounds (as cited in D. A. Carson, “Faith and Faithfulness,” Ligonier, February 1 , 20 1 0, https://learn.ligonier.org/articles/faith-and-faithfulness). There can be no true reconciliation between humans until individual sinners are first reconciled to God. The horizontal necessarily follows the vertical. Ecclesiology necessarily follows soteriology. Which is to say, the corporate element must not come first, lest we lose salvation altogether. Vertical and Horizontal But it must come. Indeed, the corporate component must remain within the structure of the doctrine of conversion itself. Our corporate unity in Christ is not just an implication of conversion; it’s part of the very thing. Being reconciled to God’s people is distinct from but inseparable from being reconciled to God. These two elements of conversion are wonderfully put on display in Ephesians 2 with two instances of the word “but.” The first comes as Paul narrates man’s rescue from sin and death (vv. 1–10), which hinges on the words “ But God, being rich in mercy . . . ” (v. 4). Those words introduce God’s saving love and the fact that he has “raised us up with [Christ] and seated us with him in the heavenly places in Christ Jesus” (v. 6). articles.content: What marks Christians attuned to cross-cultural missions? They may not serve as full-time missionaries, but they embrace Great Commission responsibilities. The history of missions reveals little-known senders who used their vocations for strategic gospel advance around the world. Captain Benjamin Wickes (1746–1830) was one such man. ‘Old Captain Wickes’ We meet this early American captain of a merchant vessel unexpectedly at a prayer meeting in 1806. The missionaries in Serampore, India, had gathered to send Henry Martyn to a station on the Ganges River where he would begin his work of translation and evangelism. Martyn recorded that they “met at my pagoda this evening for the purpose of commending me to the grace of God before my departure. My soul never before had such divine enjoyment” ( The Letters of Henry Martyn , 194). I would love to have been there. The meeting included both Baptist missionaries — William Carey, Joshua Marshman, and William Ward — as well as evangelical Anglicans David Brown, Daniel Corrie, and Henry Martyn. It represented a substantial collaboration between these earliest English missionaries for the advance of the gospel in India. Since much of India was controlled by the British East India Company, only Anglican missionaries received official recognition and freedom to travel. Even they, however, could pursue missionary work only when not employed in chaplaincy duties to English people residing in India. Amid such challenges, this prayer meeting of gathered co-laborers was a high point for Martyn and a moment he remembered fondly. To the list of those present, Martyn added “old Captain Wickes.” He mentioned him again in another letter as “the good old Captain Wickes, who has brought out so many missionaries to India” ( Letters , 178). But who was this old American captain so well loved by the English missionaries in India? Missionaries as Risky Passengers Captain Wickes was born to a seafaring family in Maryland in 1746. His older brother, Captain Lambert Wickes, fought and died at sea during the American War for Independence. Benjamin first entered the missionary record in 1799, when the Baptist missionaries Joshua Marshman and William Ward sought passage to India from London. The situation was sensitive. The East India Company had forbidden full-time missionaries from entering, so no English ship would give Marshman and Ward passage. Carey had established his home in the Danish port of Serampore, not far from Calcutta, but no Danish ships were available. Wickes’s American ship, however, could take the risk of transporting missionaries. When he heard about the situation, Wickes wrote to Baptist leader Andrew Fuller, saying that “he had long cherished the hope of being privileged to convey the messengers of the Gospel to the heathen, and that his fondest wish was about to be gratified” ( The Life and Times of Carey, Marshman, and Ward , 110). The privilege came with difficulties. Although American ships were regularly received in East India Company ports, the presence of missionaries complicated their arrival. When Wickes arrived in Calcutta with Marshman and Ward, East India Company officials refused him permission to sail home unless he took the missionaries with him. By God’s grace, Wickes convinced the authorities of the missionaries’ good intentions. When similar circumstances occurred in 1806, he persuaded officials that detaining his American ship might cause an international incident. Each voyage involved protracted negotiations that certainly distracted from his primary trading business. Yet Wickes’s service proved invaluable. Every time the missionaries mentioned him, they affirmed their unbridled thanks for his efforts. William Carey wrote about him in 1805, “I, in common with my dear brethren and sisters here, feel much pleasure in hearing of the safe return to you of our much beloved brother in Christ, Capt. Wickes” ( Evangelical Intelligencer , 1:201). Marshman and Ward called him “th

威克船长 在1806年的一次祈祷会中,我们意外地遇到了这位早期的美国商船船长. 印度塞兰波尔的传教士们聚集一堂,将亨利·马蒂恩送往恒河上的一个站,在那里他将开始翻译和福音派的工作.

Martyn记录说,他们“今晚在我的佛塔相会,目的是在我离开之前赞扬我受到上帝的恩惠。 我的灵魂从未有过如此神圣的享受”(The Letters of Henry Martyn, 194). 我很想去过那里。

与会的有浸信会传教士威廉·凯里(William Carey),约书亚·马什曼(Joshua Marshman)和威廉·沃德(William Ward)等,还有福音派圣公会教徒大卫·布朗(David Brown),丹尼尔·科里(Daniel Corrie)和亨利·马蒂恩. 它代表了这些最早的英国传教士为在印度推进福音而进行的实质性合作。

由于印度大部分地区被英国东印度公司所控制,只有英国圣公会传教士才得到官方的承认并享有出行的自由. 然而,即使他们也只能在不受雇于居住在印度的英国人担任牧师职务时才能从事传教工作。

在这样的挑战中,这次聚集的同实验室的祈祷会是马蒂恩的高潮,也是他亲切回忆的一瞬. 在出席者名单中,马蒂恩加上了“威克船长”。 他在另一封信中再次提到他,称他为“威克船长,他把这么多传教士带到了印度”(信件,178)。

但这位老美国队长 在印度的英国传教士这么爱谁? 传教士作为"冒险乘客""威克船长"于1746年生于马里兰的一个航海家庭. 他的哥哥,船长兰伯特·威克斯(Lambert Wickes)在美国独立战争中出战并死于海上.

本杰明于1799年首次入传教记录,当时浸信会传教士约书亚·马什曼和威廉·沃德从伦敦寻求通向印度. 情况很敏感。 东印度公司曾禁止全职传教士入道,因此英国船只不会给马什曼和沃德通过.

凯里在离加尔各答不远的丹麦塞兰波尔港建立了他的家,但是没有丹麦船只可供使用. 但威克斯的美国船可能承担运送传教士的风险。

当Wickes听说情况时,他写信给浸信会领袖Andrew Fuller,称“他长期以来一直珍视着有幸将福音信使传达给异教徒的希望,而且他最亲切的愿望即将得到满足”(The Life and Times of Carey, Marshman, and Ward, 110.). 特权带来了困难。

虽然美国船只经常被接收到东印度公司港口,但传教士的到来使其更加复杂. 当威克斯与马什曼和沃德一起到达加尔各答后,东印度公司官员拒绝他出航回家,除非他带着传教士一起. 在上帝的恩典下,威克说服了传教士的善意权威.

当1806年发生类似情况时,他劝说官员们,扣留他的美国船只可能造成国际事件. 每次航行都涉及旷日持久的谈判,当然分散了他的初级贸易业务。 但威克斯的服务证明是宝贵的。 每逢传教士提到他,他们都申明他们无所顾忌地感谢他的努力.

articles.title: Editor’s Pick: New Children’s Picture Books
articles.summary: Let these stories remind you to enjoy the goodness of the moment and, even as it changes to something new, that God’s goodness is everlasting.
articles.summary_zh: 让这些故事提醒你享受当下的美好，即使它变成了新的东西，神的美好是永恒的。
articles.title_zh: 编辑精选：全新儿童图画书
articles.content: Autumn is a season of changes. At our home, as the leaves yellowed and the days shortened, my youngest child started middle school. That means picture books have me feeling a little nostalgia for the past these days, right alongside a lot of excitement for new things to come. Many of these books are about big changes and adjusting to them, like living with a new baby, moving to a new place, or finding a new heart in Christ’s kingdom. But some are also about the little changes happening around us every day, like laughter over a fleeting moment of childhood imagination or settling down to sleep to prepare for a new day. With all these experiences arriving on the horizon and then flying past like interstate billboards, it’s sweet to remember that “every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of lights, with whom there is no variation or shadow due to change” (James 1:17). As you hand one of these brand-new books to a young reader or curl up to enjoy it together, let these stories remind you to enjoy the goodness of the moment, even as it is changing to something new, and that God’s goodness is everlasting. 1. God Gives Sleep by Betsy Childs Howard, illustrated by Bethan Welby ( TGC Store | Amazon) When our family was exhausted and planning a big move with four children ages 6 and under, I really could have used this little book from Betsy Childs Howard. God Gives Sleep is a rhyming board book with illustrations of adorable animals (sleeping ladybugs!) and two simple refrains that even very young listeners can repeat or “read” for themselves: “God gives sleep” and “God will keep.” Both reflect promises from God that feel vital to the early days of parenting filled with sweet, sleepy snuggles and long, sleepless nights. The last picture shows the entire family asleep and includes Isaiah 40:31 (“Those who hope in the LORD will renew their strength,” NIV). God Gives Sleep is engaging, gentle, funny, and wise, and I’ve already given it to parents of new babies. 2. Winnie-the-Pooh: The Graphic Novel by A. A. Milne, adapted by Kevan Chandler and Joe Sutphin ( Amazon ) Full disclosure: I’m a huge Pooh fan. I’ve probably read the original Milne book dozens of times, and I can be a little sniffy about adaptations. But I loved this one. While I missed Milne’s distinctive narration in parts of the storytelling, this graphic novel retains enough of the original language and has such beautiful artwork that it easily justifies its existence. Parents of young independent readers often ask me for recommendations for books complex enough to be engaging but with content and formatting suitable for early elementary school. This version perfectly fits that space where 6-to-9-year-olds can track the story through the pictures but also enjoy the challenge of some complex vocabulary (“Sudden and Temporary Immersion”) and jokes that reward context research (“An ambush is a sort of Surprise.” “So is a gorse-bush sometimes.”). Winnie-the-Pooh: The Graphic Novel is a sweet and worthy tribute to this classic celebration of early childhood in all its imaginative wonder. 3. The Upside-Down, Inside-Out, Can’t-Believe-It Kingdom by Jonathan Landry Cruse, illustrated by Joe Hox ( Amazon ) The adventure begins with a son begging his father to tell him an exciting bedtime story with dragons and knights. The result is this retelling of the gospel as a quest with a king and a prince and a reminder of our humble place in the kingdom. Joe Hox’s illustrations stand out for being traditional and bright, with a dragon that isn’t too fierce for younger readers but also enough detail within the pictures to engage older readers. The story tells us that the good King will “make us be strong with the strength of His might,” a powerful message for young knights who want to do great things for the kingdom. 4. Doing Something New: A Prayer for Beginnings by Mitali Perkins, illustrated by Andrés Landazábal ( Amazon ) Mitali Perkins includes a n
articles.content_zh:
秋为一季之变. 在家中,随着叶子被黄了,日子被缩短,我最小的孩子开始上中学. 这意味着图书让我觉得过去有些怀旧, 与很多刺激 来的新事物。

这些书中很多是关于大变化并适应它们,比如与新婴儿一起生活,搬到新地方,或者在基督的王国中找到新的心. 但有些人也谈到我们周围每天发生的小变化,比如在童年短暂的想象中欢笑,或者沉睡以准备新的一天。

随着所有这些经历的到来,然后像州际告示牌一样飞过,令人欣慰的是,“每一个好的礼物和完美的礼物都是来自上面,来自灯之父,与他一起没有变化或阴影。” (詹姆斯1:17)。

当你把这些全新的书交给一个年轻的读者 或整理起来一起欣赏的时候, 让这些故事提醒你享受这一刻的美好, 即使它正在变成新的事物, 上帝的善良是永恒的。 1. 联合国

由Bethan Welby(TGC Store QQ Amazon)所展示, 当家庭精疲力竭,计划一个大动作 四个孩子6岁和6岁以下, 我真的可以用这本小书 从贝茜 Childs Howard。

上帝赐予睡眠(God Gives Sleep)是一本配有可爱动物(sleeping ladybugs!)插图的韵律板书,还有两个简单的节奏,即使非常年轻的听众也能为自己重复或“阅读 ” : “ 上帝赐予睡眠 ” 和“上帝会保留 ” 。 两者都反映了上帝的诺言,这些诺言对养育孩子的早期至关重要,充满了甜蜜的,沉睡的和漫长的,无眠的夜晚.

最后一张图片显示整个家庭都睡了,包括以赛亚40:31(“那些希望被耶和华唤起力量的人”,NIV)。 上帝赐予睡眠的热情、温和、幽默和智慧, 由Kevan Chandler和Joe Sutphin(亚马逊)改编 全面披露:我是一个巨大的维尼粉丝。

我可能读过Milne的原作数十次, 但我爱这个 虽然我错过了Milne在故事部分的突出叙事,

年轻独立读者的家长经常向我征求关于书本复杂到足以参与,但内容和格式适合初等学校的建议。

这一版本完全适合6至9岁的人通过图片追踪故事的空间,但也享受一些复杂词汇的挑战(“突然和暂时的印象”)和奖励上下文研究的笑话(“埋伏是一种惊喜”)。 “有时粗鲁也是。 ”

Winnie-the-Pooh:"图形小说"(The Graphic Newvel)是对这一经典的幼儿期庆祝活动的甜美而值得称道的赞誉,在其所有富有想象力的奇迹中. 3. 乔纳森·兰德里·克鲁斯(Jonathan Landry Cruse)的《上下、内出、不能相信的王国》。 冒险从一个乞求父亲的儿子开始,告诉他一个令人兴奋的与龙和骑士同床共枕的故事.

结果是福音的重现 与国王和王子一起探索 并提醒我们在王国的卑微地位 乔·霍克斯的插画突出表现为传统和明亮, 龙对年轻读者来说不是太凶猛,

故事告诉我们,好国王将“以他的力量使我们强大起来”,这是希望为王国做大事的年轻骑士的有力信息。 Mitali Perkins的《为开端祈祷》, Andrés Landazábal(亚马逊) 所描述,

articles.title: How Memorizing the Sermon on the Mount Reorders My Heart
articles.summary: In a world where algorithms capture our affections and lure us online via our cravings, one of the most effective resistance strategies we can employ is to study and memorize Scripture—especially the Sermon on the Mount.
articles.summary_zh: 在一个算法捕捉我们的感情并通过我们的渴望在网上引诱我们的世界里，我们可以使用的最有效的抵抗策略之一是学习和背诵圣经，尤其是登山宝训。
articles.title_zh: 背诵登山宝训如何重塑我的心
articles.content: A couple of years ago, two college students challenged me—a woman in her 50s—to memorize the Sermon on the Mount (Matt. 5–7). Inwardly, I balked, but now I know that few things in my 35 years of following Jesus have been more transformative than committing Jesus’s most famous sermon to memory. John Stott wrote that the Sermon on the Mount is “the nearest thing to a manifesto that [Jesus] ever uttered, for it is his own description of what he wanted his followers to be and to do.” After spending the last few years memorizing it, I see with increasing clarity that I need Jesus’s help to live out what he taught. In a world where algorithms capture our affections and lure us online via our cravings, one of the most effective resistance strategies we can employ is to study and memorize Scripture—especially the Sermon on the Mount. Create a New Algorithm The algorithm often knows us better than we know ourselves. Every time we buy something on Amazon or pause to watch a reel on social media, the algorithm chronicles our activities and builds a profile of us. This profile shows our real interests (not just the ones we list in our social media bios) and some of our most private behaviors (the ones we thank God aren’t live streamed). In milliseconds, companies use what the algorithm knows about us to discover the most effective way to get us to buy their products. In the same way that the algorithm learns about us with each post we like and each reel we watch, God’s Word comes alive in us with every command we learn and put into practice, with every verse we ponder, and with every teaching we adopt as a way of life. By absorbing and obeying Jesus’s Sermon on the Mount, we can create a feedback loop that enlarges his kingdom rule over our lives. Let Scripture Reorder Your Heart Before I started my memorization project, I’d heard many Christians tout Scripture memory as one of the most potent tools for conforming to Jesus, but I didn’t take it seriously. All that changed when I realized algorithms had more access to my life than God’s Word did. By absorbing and obeying Jesus’s Sermon on the Mount, we can create a feedback loop that enlarges his kingdom rule over our lives. Like many Americans, I was averaging more than two hours daily scrolling social media and shopping online, and much less time reading the Bible. I’d thought lack of time was my biggest obstacle to memorizing Scripture. But in reality, my affections and priorities were the obstacle. Memorizing and studying the Sermon on the Mount has provided a powerful reset. I’ve noticed two significant changes in my life. 1. My thoughts are increasingly populated by Jesus’s desires for me. Previously, I was easily shaped by what internet influencers said I should be doing and what my heart really wanted to do. Now, Scripture tenderly draws me to Christ’s transforming grace. For example, a few months ago, someone wrote harsh words to me. I couldn’t sidestep what I’d memorized: Pray for those who hurt you (Mt. 5:44) In those difficult interactions, Jesus’s teaching gave me wisdom to stop reacting and start praying for the one lashing out. Pausing to pray breaks down my self-protective stance so I can consider what the log in my eye might be (Mt. 7:5). 2. I see how vastly different God’s kingdom is from the world we live in. I no longer feel as drawn to the shallow version of perfection the algorithm offers me—the beautiful home, the perfectly fit woman charmingly dressed, or the promise of perpetual travel. When I stop to linger over another picture-perfect kitchen, the Sermon on the Mount prompts me to consider where my treasure really is. These chapters have given me a robust lens through which I can view all of God’s Word. After drinking so deeply of Jesus’s sermon , I see it as the hinge on which both the Old Testament and the New Testament hang. I had thought lack of time was my biggest obstacle to memorizing Scripture. But in reality, my affections and priorities were the obstacl
articles.content_zh:
几年前,两个大学生挑战我——一个50多岁的女性——要记住山上赛门(Matt. 5-7). 但现在我知道,在我追随耶稣的35年里, 没有什么事情比把耶稣最出名的布道当作记忆更具有变革性。

约翰·斯托特(John Stott)写道:"山上赛蒙是[耶稣]曾经发表的宣言中最接近的东西,因为这是他自己对追随者所希望的和所要做的事的描述". 我越来越清楚地看到,我需要耶稣的帮助来维持他所教的。

在一个算法捕捉到我们感情并通过我们的渴望来引诱我们上线的世界中,我们可以采用的最有效的抵抗策略之一是学习并记住"圣经"——特别是"山上"的"塞尔门". 创建新算法 算法常常比我们自己更了解我们.

每次我们购买亚马逊或暂停观看社交媒体的片段, 算法记录我们的活动, 以及一些最私人的行为(我们感谢上帝的人不是活生生的)。

在毫秒内,公司利用算法了解我们的情况,发现最有效的方法让我们购买他们的产品. 正如算法用我们所喜欢的每一个帖子和我们所看的每一卷片子来了解我们一样,上帝的言语以我们所学习和运用的每一个命令、我们所思考的每一个诗句和我们所采纳的作为生活方式的每一个教义,在我们中充满活力。

通过吸收和服从耶稣在"山上"的赛蒙,我们可以建立一个反馈回路,扩大他的王国对我们生活的统治. 在开始我的回忆计划之前, 我听到许多基督徒将圣经记忆说成是符合耶稣的最有力工具之一,

当我意识到算法与上帝的言语相比, 通过吸收和服从耶稣在"山上"的赛蒙,我们可以建立一个反馈回路,扩大他的王国对我们生活的统治. 我和许多美国人一样,平均每天有两个多小时 滚动社交媒体和网上购物, 阅读圣经的时间要少得多。

我本以为没有时间是我记起圣经的最大障碍。 但实际上,我的爱和优先考虑是障碍。 纪念并研究了"山上"的"塞尔门"提供了强大的重置. 我注意到我生命中有两个重大的变化。 1. 耶稣对我的渴望使我的思想日益丰富。

之前,我很容易被网络影响者 说我应该做什么 和我的心真正想要做什么。 现在,《圣经》轻而易举地吸引我走向基督的恩典。 例如,几个月前,有人给我写了严厉的话. 我无法回避我所记住的:为伤害你的人祈祷(Mt.

5:44 在困难的交往中,耶稣的教导给了我智慧,让我停止反应,开始为那一次狂欢祈祷. 暂停祈祷 打破自我保护的姿势 这样我就可以考虑我的眼中可能是什么(7:5山) 2. 我看到上帝的王国与我们生活的世界大相径庭。

我不再觉得算法能吸引到我的 浅薄的完美版本, 当我停止停留 停留在另一个图片完美的厨房, 山上赛门 促使我考虑 我的宝藏到底在哪里。

这些章节给了我一个强烈的透镜,我可以透视上帝的所有言语。 在饮用耶稣的布道之后,我认为这是旧约和新约所依赖的。 我以为没有时间 是我记起圣经的最大障碍 但实际上,我的爱和优先 是迷信

articles.title: ‘Young Man, You Look Miserable’
articles.summary: God changed the heart of a young “prince of preachers” all with a single, simple verse: Look to Jesus and live. Watch Now
articles.summary_zh: 神用一句简单的诗句改变了一位年轻的“传道者之王”的心：仰望耶稣，活下去。现在观看
articles.title_zh: ‘年轻人，你看起来很悲惨’
articles.content: I’m excited to tell you the story of how God used a simple verse, from a complicated passage, to change the life of a man named Charles Spurgeon. His story is for everyone, but it may have a special word to speak to a few groups in the room. One is laymen — that is, people who work for a living in normal jobs, outside of Christian ministry. People without a seminary education, people who aren’t pastors or have ministry jobs. We recognize that this series has profiled four men who were preachers. Now, there is an interesting flow to our series: - first, Saint Augustine, - then, Luther, who was an Augustinian monk, - then, John Bunyan, whose favorite book outside the Bible was Luther’s commentary on Galatians, - now, Charles Spurgeon, whose favorite book outside the Bible was Bunyan’s Pilgrim’s Progress. We’ve moved from one convert to another, each building in some way on the previous one, but a weakness of our series (in some sense) is that they all became preachers. And we don’t expect you all to become preachers; we’d like a few, but most will be laymen, and that’s good. Now, Spurgeon is known as “the Prince of Preachers.” But the hero, under God, in Spurgeon’s story is not Spurgeon, and not a trained, paid preacher, but a layman. So, Spurgeon’s story has a special word for laymen who are willing to open their mouths and say what they know about Jesus. Spurgeon’s story also has a special word for teens and young adults. Spurgeon came to faith at age fifteen, which in his day was far more like young adulthood. Still, his story offers a challenge to those who are no longer children and not yet established adults: teens, college students, grad students, even young professionals. Don’t let the world (or the church) lower your standards of what’s possible in being deeply converted and dedicated to Jesus — and how God can make his Son thrilling to a young soul. My prayer is that God might be pleased to give some their own engine. So often, parents, college workers, and pastors help young adults along and give them pushes. And then sometimes, God is pleased in the life of teenagers to give them their own engine, and they don’t need any more pushing. They say, “Get out of my way! I am going to follow Jesus. You can’t keep me from him and worship, my Bible, and prayer!” That’s what God did for Spurgeon at age fifteen — he gave him his own engine. And I pray he might be pleased to do that even here this morning. Spurgeon’s story speaks to one more group: those in the room who are willing to admit, “I’m here but I’m not saved.” For two thousand years, unsaved people have shown up at churches for all sorts of reasons. That’s Spurgeon’s story. He was searching. He was unsaved and in a church on a Sunday morning when God broke through. So, if you’d say this morning, “I haven’t settled the issue of my sin and rebellion against God,” or “I haven’t ‘been saved,’” or “if I died on the drive home today, I wouldn’t be at peace with my Maker,” this story has a special word for you. So, let me tell you about Charlie Spurgeon. His Early and Whole Life He was born in 1834, about 40 miles northeast of London, into a Christian family. In fact, both his father and grandfather were pastors. But his father met financial troubles and sent the young Charles to live with his grandparents from ages one to six. I don’t think this is an insignificant part of the story; don’t underestimate the effects of a good grandma and grandpa in the lives of our children. From their influence he emerged as “precocious,” learned to read, and first found Bunyan’s Pilgrim’s Progress (which he would read more than a hundred times). From his earliest days, he was unusually sharp, ahead of his age level, “always reading books” (Spurgeon: A Biography, 8). He returned home at age six and excelled at school in both math and reading. He was noticed for “his unusual mental ability and his rare clarity of speech” (10), including “his native audacity” (11), that is, his courage to say

我非常兴奋地向大家讲述上帝如何用一段简单的诗句, 从一段复杂的段落中, 他的故事是针对每个人的,但可能有一个特别的单词,可以和房间里的几个团体交谈. 一个是外行者,也就是在基督教部之外从事正常工作谋生的人。

没有神学院教育的人, 我们承认,这一系列的描述 4人谁是传道者。

现在,我们的系列有一个有趣的流传:首先,圣奥古斯丁, 然后,路德,他是一个奥古斯丁的修道士, 然后,约翰·邦扬,他最喜欢的书是路德对加拉提安的评论, 现在,查尔斯·斯普吉翁,他最喜欢的书是"邦扬朝圣者的进步"。

但我们系列的一个弱点(某种意义上的)就是他们都成了传教士。 我们并不期望你们都成为传教士;我们想做几个,但多数是外行,这很好。

现在,斯普吉翁被称为"道教的王子". 但是,在上帝的统治下,在斯普吉翁的故事里,英雄不是斯普吉翁,也不是一个受过训练,有报酬的传教士,而是一名外行人. 因此,斯普吉恩的故事有一个特别的词来形容那些愿意张开口子,说出自己对耶稣所了解的. Spurgeon的故事中也有一个针对青少年和年轻成年人的特殊词.

斯普吉安在15岁时开始信仰,在他这一天,这更像是年轻的成年. 然而,他的故事给那些已经不是孩子和还没有成年的人带来了挑战:青少年,大学生,研究生,甚至年轻专业人员.

不要让世界(或教会)降低你对于什么是可能的, 我的祷告是 上帝可能很乐意 给一些自己的引擎。 父母、大学员工和牧师经常帮助年轻的成年人并给予他们推动。

有时,上帝在青少年生活中很高兴给他们自己的引擎,他们不需要再再推了. 他们说:你们离我远点! 我要跟随耶稣。 你无法阻止我远离他, 这是上帝在15岁时为斯波克森所做的——他给了他自己的引擎. 我祈求他今天上午也乐意这么做

Spurgeon的故事又讲述了一个群体:那些在房间里愿意承认“我在这里,但我没有被拯救。 ” 两千年来,无所救护的人出于各种原因都出现在了教堂. 这是斯普吉恩的故事。 他在寻找。 周日早上,上帝破门而入时,他被解剖,在教堂里。

所以,如果你今天上午说,“我还没有解决我的罪恶和反抗上帝的问题,”或者“我还没有`拯救',或者“如果我今天在回家的路上死了,我也不会与我的造物主和睦相处,”这个故事有一个特别的词给你。 让我告诉你查理·斯波克森的事 他于1834年生于伦敦东北约40英里处,进入基督教家庭.

事实上,他的父亲和祖父都是牧师。 但是他的父亲遇到了财政上的困难,并派年轻的查尔斯从一到六岁就和外祖父母住在一起. 我并不认为这是故事的次要部分,

从他们的影响力中,他出现了“珍贵的,”学会了阅读,并首先发现了邦扬的"朝圣者进步"(他将读一百多遍)。 从他最初的年代起,他就异常尖锐地领先于他的年龄,"总是阅读书籍"("外科医生:一部传记",8). 他六岁回家,在学校数学和阅读方面都非常出色。

他因“他不寻常的智力和他罕有的言语清晰度”而被注意(10个),包括“他的本地胆识”(11个),即他的勇气说:

articles.title_zh: 五个辅导失误和圣灵的帮助
articles.content: As we were finishing a counseling session, Jill looked at me with concern, her eyebrows furrowed. “You got distracted,” she bluntly stated. Unfortunately, Jill was right. Just outside my workspace, several pastors gathered in the church office lobby, talking and laughing. I’d gotten sidetracked by the commotion. About 70 percent of me was attending to Jill, but 30 percent of my headspace had shifted to the lobby: What are they doing? What’s so funny? We live in a distractible culture. Between YouTube shorts and checking our email inboxes every hour, our minds wander quickly. Staying focused is a skill few truly master. But it’s essential if we’re going to care well for God’s people. Whether formally or informally, counseling another soul is a distinct privilege. Yet, too often, mistakes plague our conversations. Fortunately, getting distracted is one of several common mistakes that are correctable. After Jill’s jarring comment, I closed the window blinds (simple fix), talked to the staff about keeping the commotion down (another simple fix), recommitted to staying focused (possible, though it would be work), and prayed the Lord would renew my love for his sheep. What counseling mistakes are you prone to make? Take a quick check. Mistake 1: Fear of Man Charlotte shares about her struggles with her job. She dislikes her boss, and she’s weary of her work. Unfortunately, she often responds to her difficulties with sinful choices. This time, she lied to her boss to get out of an assignment. You sympathize with her frustrations but feel convinced you’ve got to speak up about her lying. Charlotte’s a Christian, and Scripture makes clear that because God never lies, Christ’s followers shouldn’t either (Colossians 3:9–10; Titus 1:2). Yet you hesitate. You know Charlotte will get angry, and your fears kick in. Why bother bringing it up? Lying is between her and God. Right now, she needs a friend. But you know if you don’t say something, Charlotte will eventually lie to her boss again. What should you do? Repent of your fear that causes you to avoid a difficult word. Confess your worry about speaking up to the Lord (Psalm 34:4). If you struggle with people-pleasing, then saying a difficult word will feel painful. Reframe your situation by putting the fear of God at the center of your thinking (Proverbs 29:25; Luke 12:4–5). If we fear God more than Charlotte, we won’t let Charlotte’s potential anger get in the way. My friend Jonathan Leeman calls the helper in this situation a “sin-absorber.” A true friend willingly absorbs the cost of another person’s sin for the sake of honoring Christ. Would you be willing to absorb Charlotte’s anger if it helps her address her lie? Mistake 2: Assumed Insight Angela and John have been married for 31 years. Sometimes John gets frustrated with Angela because she assumes what he’s thinking. “I know I’m not supposed to assume,” Angela would think, “but we’ve been together for a long time.” The more familiar you are with someone, the more you’re likely to get in trouble. Familiarity breeds assumptions . Think about your last conflict. How many assumptions did you make? Probably a few. Assumptions can create problems. Sometimes our assumptions are true, but often they’re not. If you’re prone to making assumptions, here’s how to stay away from trouble: Don’t overestimate your ability to size up a situation. Pride makes you think, “I know what’s going on.” Humility tells you, “Ask God for wisdom.” The humble recognize they’re not as smart as they think and must depend on the Lord for insight (James 1:5). After you’ve asked the Lord for help, test your assumptions. Don’t tolerate any of them. Check the validity of your assumptions by asking thoughtful, careful, and loving questions. Genuine curiosity will lead you to ask rather than assume. At the encouragement of a friend, Angela asked more questions during marital conflict, and that built more understanding between her and John. The apostle Paul tells us that

articles.title: 当精神疾病成为身份标签
articles.summary: 当精神疾病成为身份标签，最需要帮助的人会不会反而被忽视？《都在你脑中》批评了浪漫化疾病、自我诊断和社交媒体追逐关注的风气。
articles.content: 弗雷德里克·德波尔（Frederik deBoer）曾因双相情感障碍被强制送进精神医疗机构。此后几年，他心里一直交织着两种感受：一方面，他由衷感激这个救了自己一命的医疗体系；另一方面，看到如今很少有人能像他一样得到帮助并慢慢康复，他又深感沮丧。 《都在你脑中：疾病成为身份、创伤成为时尚，以及对患病的渴望》（ All in Your Head: Illness as Identity, Trauma as Fashion, and the Desire to Be Disordered ）是他的最新力作。德波尔活跃于网络，常跟主流观点唱反调，自称“老派”马克思主义者，他最出名的一本书是《聪明崇拜》（ The Cult of Smart ）。这一次，他把批评的矛头对准了自己所属的阵营，该阵营里一些文化观念的变化反而让最需要精神医疗的人更难得到帮助。他写道：“多年来一直让我恼火的一件事，就是把精神疾病当成一场刺激的冒险，以及流行文化对精神失常没完没了的浪漫化。”（8 页） 让他恼火的是，人们把精神疾病和功能障碍当成值得庆祝的身份，而不是需要治疗的问题。他的担忧并非空穴来风。从 2019 年 到 2024 年 ，谈话治疗的使用增长了 47%。 LifeStance在 2025 年开展的一项调查 发现，约 29%的美国成年人曾根据看到的网络内容，自行判断自己患有某种心理疾病；在Z世代中，这一比例高达 50%，而婴儿潮一代只有 9%。而在这些人里，近四分之一（24%）“很少”或“从不”觉得有必要再去找合格的临床专业人员聊一聊。 德波尔认为，社会过度关注那些症状轻微、甚至是否患病都不确定的人，结果非但没减少人们对精神疾病的偏见，反而转移了注意力，挤占了重症患者获得帮助的机会。他把这种现象称为“障碍的士绅化”：处于优势地位的人占据了讨论的中心，真正处境艰难的患者却被挤到了边缘。社交媒体的推波助澜，让这股风气全面爆发、像传染病一样蔓延，甚至连负责精神医疗的专家和机构也失去了公信力（153–154 页）。 德波尔的判断大体正确。他指出的文化变化，在教会内外都产生了实实在在的影响。不过，使他的批评如此尖锐的思想立场，也让他留下了两个重要的盲点。如果能正视这些盲点，《都在你脑中》就会更勇敢、更有建设性，也更可能被广泛阅读，成为我们需要的那个有力宣言。 《 都在你脑中：疾病成为身份、创伤成为时尚，以及对患病的渴望 》（ All in Your Head: Illness as Identity, Trauma as Fashion, and the Desire to be Disordered ） 弗雷德里克·德波尔（Frederik deBoer）著 在《都在你脑中》中，德波尔对当代心理健康文化提出了有力的批评，这样的批评早就该出现了。他指出，“去机构化”原本是为了纠正早期精神医疗中的虐待问题，出发点虽好，最终却酿成人道灾难，使严重精神疾病患者在流落街头、遭到监禁和无人照管的处境中反复辗转。 近年来，“障碍的士绅化”又让精神疾病成了社交资本，而那些受疾病影响最严重的人，却仍在街头每况愈下。数字时代进一步加剧了这场危机：社交媒体传播着难以置信的自我诊断，人们借罕见疾病展示自己的特殊身份，真正患病者的声音反而无人倾听。 西蒙与舒斯特出版社（Simon & Schuster），336 页。 左右两派都在批评之列 如果你拿起《都在你脑中》，是想弄明白过去几年现代治疗文化怎么像野火一样在社交媒体上蔓延，那德波尔一上来就深入分析 20 世纪晚期反精神病学运动对政治和学术界的影响，你大概会有点摸不着头脑。不过，他的“疯狂”自有章法。 他先把忽视精神疾病的“右翼自由意志主义”政策狠狠批了一通，借此赢得左倾读者的信任，然后掉转枪口，一记记重拳砸向“一种有时近乎左翼伪激进主义或自由意志主义幻想的思维方式”（198 页）。正是这种思维，推动了“从把精神疾病当作现实，到把它当作象征的颠覆性转变”（8 页）。 美国的个人主义和反建制偏见并不新鲜，但德波尔极为细致地追踪了它们在精神健康与治疗文化中如何蔓延，读来令人耳目一新，也很有启发。 无论政治立场如何，人们都可能对“反抗现代社会”抱有浪漫的想象，而这又滋生了两种相反的错误。在右派眼中，精神疾病有时被看成是想象出来的问题，或是性格软弱的表现。在左派那里，同样的浪漫想象却常把精神障碍说成一种优势，仿佛它带给人的能力多于限制；仿佛那些认知和思维方式与多数人不同的少数群体不需要社会帮助，反倒是社会需要他们的帮助。 当“障碍”成为优势群体的身份标签 德波尔坚决反对“把医学上的疾病变成身份认同”。他将反对这种主要盛行于进步派的错误，视为“全书的总原则”（165 页）。他对“障碍的士绅化”的分析，最鲜明地体现了这一点。原本关心病情最严重者的研究与公共讨论，如今却围着一群症状轻微、甚至是否患病都存疑的人打转，结果“诊断成了时尚”（154 页）。 为什么这些讨论和相关机构会如此偏离初衷？德波尔指出，一方面是“社交媒体扭曲的激励机制”，另一方面则是自由派普遍接受的一种观念，“只要有人声称自己有某种障碍，质疑他的说法就是冒犯。”两者结合，“我们便创造出了一个个‘病症群体’”，与那些“支持某支球队”的球迷俱乐部相差无几（154 页）。 那些经济条件较好，或仍保有较强生活能力、能够在网上展示自身障碍的人，得到了过多关注。这种注意力的偏移带来了切实的后果：有影响力的精英越是凭借自己的地位，“界定公众心目中这种障碍的模样”，那些贫困或障碍严重的人就越容易被忽视，得不到照顾。 过去十年，只要稍微留意周围的变化，就会觉得这些现象十分眼熟。正如我在《 我们为何需要教会 》（The Reason for Church）中所说，社交媒体这类冒充传统机构角色的平台，绕过了原有的把关机制，也扭曲了那些支撑美国社会与属灵生活的重要机构的运作动机。 在帮助我们辨认这些现象方面，《都在你脑中》未必提供了多少新见解。德波尔的贡献，在于以一个“脾气暴躁的老马克思主义者”的眼光，追踪这些现象如何遍布错综复杂的官僚体系。他不满于通俗化批判理论和进步派政治中的虚伪，尤其是那些享有特权却又置身其中的人。这一视角固然有用，但同样的思想立场也限制了他的分析，留下两个明显的缺口。 诊断不完整，药方也不足 他最明显的遗漏，是性别焦虑诊断与未成年人性别重置手术的迅速增加。十多年来，一些提供性别肯定治疗的医生不断告诉父母，他们必须在“一个跨性别孩子”和“一个死去的孩子”之间作出选择。但丽贝卡·麦克劳克林（Rebecca McLaughlin）根据相关证据，对这种说法 提出了质疑 ：“青春期阻断剂可能使一些年轻人的心理健康状况更糟，而不是更好。” 德波尔一向敢于在自己的阵营中提出不受欢迎、挑战主流的观点，这一点令人佩服。正因如此，他竟然没有讨论有害心理治疗文化所带来的、堪称最具争议也最可能改变人一生的后果，实在令人费解。 第二个遗漏则比较容易理解。他在结尾提出了一些论证充分的政策建议，尽管令人遗憾的是，这些建议建立在唯物主义与社会主义的基础上。然而，对于更广泛的心理治疗文化，他却没有提出解决办法。这种文化执着于“激进的个人自主观念”（77 页），而他在书中用了大量篇幅，论证这正是人们抗拒改革的根源。不处理这个问题，就使他的政策建议大大失去了说服力。 基督徒可以认同德波尔对个人自主观念的批评。不过，教会拥有立法和政策方案所不能提供的群体生活与属灵资源。我们知道，人受造并不是要靠自己塑造身份，而是要在基督里，在与家庭、教会以及最终与神的关系中，认识自己是谁。 尽管有所遗漏，《都在你脑中》仍是一本观察清醒、引起读者共鸣的书，尤其适合那些正在接受精神医疗、或对其感到失望的人。它很适合与马修·洛夫特斯（Matthew Loftus）的《 抵挡心理治疗文化 》（ Resisting Therapy Culture ）搭配阅读。书中描述的许多问题，也是菲利普·里夫（Philip Rieff）在《心理治疗的胜利》（ The Triumph of the Therapeutic ）中早已预见的后果。 《都在你脑中》“不是一本回忆录”（8 页）。它打破了回忆录的写法，把目光投向亟待解决的现实问题。全书充满了出于正义感的愤慨，既批评把精神疾病当成表演的风气，也批评助长这种表演的窥探欲。德波尔由此为我们梳理出当代心理健康文化的来龙去脉，具体而有力，也让许多令人困惑的现象有了解释。 原文刊载于福音联盟英文网站： Beware Making Mental Illness an Identity .

articles.title: 跟随爱任纽，读懂使徒所传的福音
articles.summary: 二世纪牧者爱任纽带领我们沿着使徒的教导，认识三一真神，并从旧约中看见基督。即使有些解释不能全盘接受，他的著作仍值得今天的基督徒认真阅读。
articles.content: 基督徒有时会忘记我们的信仰有多么悠久的历史。当然，我们都知道，耶稣在两千年前降世、受 死、复活。但我们容易忘记，两千年来，一代又一代基督徒敬拜祂、思想祂，为祂而活、为祂而死，也写下了许多关于祂的文字。 对今天的我们来说，那些最早期的基督徒，他们所生活的世界既遥远又陌生，却很值得走近、了解。我推荐从里昂的爱任纽（Irenaeus of Lyons）所著的《使徒式讲道》（ On the Apostolic Preaching ）读起。圣弗拉基米尔神学院出版社（St. Vladimir’s Seminary Press）的“大众教父文库”（Popular Patristics）收录了一个不错的现代英语译本。这本书篇幅不长，共 101 页；若不算译者约翰·贝尔（John Behr）所写的长篇导论，正文只有 63 页，读起来也不算艰深。 《使徒式讲道》（ On the Apostolic Preaching ） 里昂的爱任纽（St Irenaeus of Lyons）著 圣弗拉基米尔神学院出版社，121 页。 里昂的爱任纽 爱任纽生活在公元二世纪后期。年轻时，他住在士每拿，也就是今天土耳其西部的伊兹密尔，曾受教于一位名叫坡旅甲（Polycarp）的牧者。而坡旅甲本人，曾直接受教于使徒约翰！爱任纽后来这样回忆： 他（坡旅甲）常谈起自己与约翰，以及其他亲眼见过主的人之间的亲密交往，也常回忆他们所说的话。凡是从他们那里听到的，无论是主的神迹还是教导，他都会一一述说。坡旅甲从这些亲眼见过生命之道的人那里领受的见证，全都与圣经相符。 爱任纽接着说：“因着神赐给我的怜悯，我当时留心聆听这些事，并将它们珍藏在心里。”（残篇二，《尼西亚前期教父文集》〔ANF〕第 1 卷，568 页） 后来，爱任纽迁居罗马帝国西部边陲的高卢，来到卢格杜努姆（Lugdunum），也就是今天法国的里昂（Lyons）。他在那里牧会，直到生命终了。他鼓励教会度过逼迫，向信奉异教的凯尔特人传福音，也教导基督徒抵挡诺斯替派异端。 诺斯替派对教会构成严重威胁，因此，驳斥他们的教导成了爱任纽事工的一项重点。诺斯替派教师善于曲解圣经，为自己的信仰体系寻找根据。他们教导说，圣经中的神并非至高的真神，而是一个较低等、邪恶的“神”；物质世界是他创造的，因此也是邪恶的。在他们看来，神的儿子成为人，更是不可想象的事。这些诡诈的教导，使许多基督徒偏离真理。爱任纽用了一个贴切的比喻，说明他们怎样滥用圣经： 一位技艺精湛的艺术家，用珍贵的宝石拼成了一幅美丽的君王像。他们的做法，就像有人把这幅画像完全拆散，重新排列宝石，拼成一条狗或一只狐狸，而且拼得十分拙劣。（《驳异端》〔Against Heresies〕第一卷，八章，第1节；《尼西亚前期教父文集》第 1 卷，326 页） 按照使徒的教导读圣经 身为牧者，爱任纽的一项重要心愿，就是帮助人读圣经时，始终看清那幅君王的画像。单单读圣经还不够，我们还必须按照使徒所教导的方式来读。他把正确理解圣经所依据的信仰纲要称为“信仰准则”。 我们受洗时所宣认的，正是这信仰准则：我们受洗“是奉父的名，……奉那位道成肉身、受死并复活的神子耶稣基督的名，也奉圣灵之名”（《使徒式讲道》，42 页）。在这本书中，爱任纽说明，我们怎样持守这信仰准则，在读经时始终看清君王的形象——认识那位是圣父、圣子、圣灵的独一真神，以及祂赐给我们的救恩。 圣父 针对诺斯替派的教导，爱任纽着重阐明圣经关于圣父的真理：祂是独一、至高的真神，是万有的创造主，而且祂是良善的（44 页）。 接着，他沿着旧约的叙事梳理救赎历史。他指出，对整个堕落的受造世界而言，圣父是“审判者，因为没有人能逃脱祂的审判”（45 页）；对犹太人而言，祂也是“主和赐律法者”，要他们认识祂，“昼夜向祂献上敬拜”（44–45 页）。最后，“对基督徒而言，祂是父，因为在‘末后的日子’，祂开启了使人得蒙收纳成为儿子的约”（44 页）。 耶稣基督 爱任纽说圣父至高无上，并不是把圣父置于圣子之上。他说得很清楚：“父是主，子也是主；父是神，子也是神，因为从神所生的就是神。这样，就祂的存在、能力、本质而言，所显明的乃是一位神。”（71 页）父与子（以及圣灵）各自都是真神，又共同是一位神。 同时，他这样描述圣父与圣子的区别：“但就我们得救的经世安排（economy）而言，有父，也有子。万有之父是受造之物无法看见、无法接近的，因此，凡要亲近神的人，都必须借着子来到父面前。”（71 页）爱任纽从“我们得救的安排”来说明三一神各位格之间的区别。后来的教父进一步厘清三位一体的教义，更准确地区分了神的“本体”（ontology）与“经世”（economy）：前者关乎神本身所是，以及父、子、圣灵之间永恒的关系；后者关乎三一神如何向我们启示自己、施行救赎。要求爱任纽达到后来教义表述的精确程度，并不公平。不过，他对神的理解仍是正统的：圣子是真神，与圣父为一，却又有别于圣父。圣父差遣圣子，是为要拯救我们。 重整：基督重新走过人类的道路 爱任纽常用“重整”（recapitulation）来描述耶稣拯救我们的使命。他的意思是耶稣成为人，来到世上，重新走过人类的道路，为我们成就我们未能做到的事。 要理解爱任纽所说的“重整”，需要先看他怎样理解人按神的形象受造。神“将自己的样式刻画在祂手所造的作品〔即人类〕上，使这看得见的受造物能像神；因为人是按神的形象被塑造，并被安置在地上的”（46 页）。人按神的形象受造，领受神所赐的生命和能力，因此“人像神……要管理地上的一切”（47 页）。但罪使人类与赐生命的神隔绝，不能再按受造的本分反映神的样式、治理世界，反而落在死亡的权势之下（50 页）。 为了挽回堕落的人类，耶稣“在末后的日子，为要重整万有，成为人，来到人间，成为可见、可触摸的，为要废除死亡、彰显生命，并使神与人相交”（43–44 页）。 神与人之所以能够相交，唯独因为“道成了肉身”。神的儿子取了人性，重新走过人类的道路。他取了肉身，“为要借着这曾被罪掌控、占据、辖制的肉身，除灭罪，使罪不再存于我们里面”（60 页）。这就是耶稣成为像亚当一样之人的原因，他要“在亚当里，击败那在亚当里击倒我们的仇敌”（61 页）。 爱任纽用全书的大部分篇幅，梳理那些预指耶稣的旧约经文。这些经文指向的那一位，将“在这世代的末了，以人的身份向全世界显现，在自己里面‘重整万有’”（60 页）。这些经文，都是先知“借着圣灵”所说、所写的（60 页）。 圣灵 论到圣灵，爱任纽主要强调，先知是“借着祂说预言”的。但他也提到，圣灵“在末后的日子，以新的方式浇灌在人类身上，在全世界更新人，使人归向神”（44 页）。 因为有“圣灵不断住在”我们里面，基督徒才能保守“身体不受玷污”，使“灵魂不被罪败坏”。基督徒将来的复活，也出于圣灵的工作：“身体重新与灵魂结合，并与灵魂一同靠圣灵的大能复起，被领进神的国。”（67 页） 阅读时需要分辨的地方 爱任纽读旧约时，始终注视着那幅君王的画像。他在一些经文中看见了耶稣，而今天的基督徒未必会这样理解。 他的释经多采用预表的方式，不止于考察原初读者所处的历史情境，也从经文细节所呈现的主题中，寻找指向耶稣的线索。许多解释并不难接受，例如，他认为耶稣应验了《诗篇》45 篇（71 页）、110 篇（72 页）、《以赛亚书》7 章（74–75 页）、《以赛亚书》9 章（76–77 页）、《弥迦书》5 章（81 页）等经文中的预言。不过，即使在这些经文中，他对某些细节的解释也可能令人诧异。 至于他如何在《诗篇》3 篇（87 页）、89 篇（88 页）、《耶利米哀歌》4 章（85–86 页）、《阿摩司书》9 章（81 页）等经文中看见耶稣，我们可能就更难认同了。他还引用了次经《巴录书》（Baruch）（100 页），以及一些在现存抄本中找不到的《耶利米书》段落（89 页，另见注 199）。这些都是阅读时需要留意的问题。 不过，在轻率否定爱任纽的释经之前，我们需要考虑几点。 第一，即使一段经文在原本的历史处境中并不是在讲耶稣，爱任纽从中看见耶稣，也不等于他忽略了历史背景。他只是着重指出其中那些预示耶稣的主题。 第二，我们必须记得，圣经的每一段经文都出于人的作者，也出于神这位作者。圣灵借着人说话时，所顾念的是整本圣经的全貌。因此，经文可能包含圣灵所要表达的更深含义，而人的作者既未曾想到，也未曾意识到。 第三，爱任纽所用的解经方法，也是使徒在新约中指出旧约如何指向耶稣时经常采用的方法。坦白说，我们也常常难以理解，新约作者为什么那样解释旧约经文，例如《马太福音》2:15。他们甚至会引用七十士译本，从希腊文译文中引出希伯来文原文并不明显的含义，例如《希伯来书》10:5。 当然，爱任纽不是使徒，他的著作并不具有新约圣经那样的权威与无误性。有些地方，他确实可能解释错了，我们完全可以不同意。但别忘了，他曾受教于坡旅甲，而坡旅甲把约翰的教导传给了他。想到这一点，我们至少应当认真考虑他的解释。 向这位古代牧者学习 我们或许不会同意爱任纽的每一种解释——我自己就有不同意的地方！但他教导我们，读圣经时要始终看清那幅君王的画像。在这方面，书中仍有许多值得学习之处。 这位古代的敬虔牧者深爱神的话，也深爱神的子民，因为他深爱那位是圣父、圣子、圣灵的神。他留下的智慧，至今仍能使我们受益。 原文刊载于加拿大福音联盟英文网站： On the Apostolic Preaching .

articles.title: 一封写给年轻传道人的信
articles.summary: 牧养事务繁忙，年轻传道人怎样才能忠心传讲神的话？
articles.content: 亲爱的年轻传道人： 四十年前我刚开始牧会，那时我是一间乡村教会的唯一牧者。尽管总觉得每三天就是一个主日，但是传讲神的话语给我带来极大的喜乐。感谢神，祂让我服侍一群心地宽厚、支持牧者的会众，使我这个年轻牧者有机会不断学习、成长。 刚开始事奉时我没有收到资深传道人的来信。不过，如果当时有人写信，用以下五点来勉励我，我一定会受益匪浅。这些话主要写给年轻传道人，但对所有传讲神话语的人，也是很好的提醒。 保守你的心 神在创造中设立了一个规律：生命各从其类，繁衍生息（创 1:11）。正如耶稣所说：“凡学成了的不过和先生一样。”（路 6:40）如果我们盼望借着讲道，使人越来越有基督的样式，自己就必须不断成长，越来越像基督。 读神学院时，韩君时（Howard Hendricks）博士曾提醒我们：“你自己没有的，就无法给别人。”我鼓励你，不要让灵修只是为了预备讲章；要在准备讲章之外，继续追求与神更深的相交。记住，讲道不仅需要在讲章上下功夫，也需要 在自己的心上下功夫 。“你要保守你心，胜过保守一切。”（箴 4:23） 把状态最好的时间留给讲章预备 我不是说要把所有时间都用来备讲章。身为牧者，你的职责不只是讲道。神也呼召你牧养祂的羊群，带领祂的百姓。 无论会众多少，牧养事奉的要求都可能令人身心俱疲。事实上，我独自在一间较小的教会牧会时，反而感到压力更大。不过，即使其他牧养工作同样必要、同样重要，也不要让它们挤掉你预备讲道的时间。 正如保罗劝勉年轻的提摩太：“你要以宣读、劝勉、教导为念。”（提前 4:13）要 建立一种节奏 ，把一天中状态最好的时段留给祷告和研读神的话语（徒 6:4）。牧者的确不能只满足于讲好道，但至少必须把道讲好。 给讲章预备设定截止时间 有句话是这样的，给一项工作多少时间，它就会占满多少时间。我在加拿大西部牧会时，只需要在周五早上交出讲章提纲。结果，我常常到了周四下午，还在赶着完成讲章。 后来，我到渥太华的大都会圣经教会（The Metropolitan Bible Church）担任牧师，办公室同工要求我在周四早上交出提纲。没想到，我很快就适应了，提纲和讲章初稿都比以前更早完成。虽然一周的后半段，我仍会审阅、修改讲章，但把截止时间设在周中，确实提高了预备效率。 设立截止时间，真的能带来改变。即使没有人要求你在某个特定时候完成讲章，也要给自己定一个期限。 讲道既要劝勉，也要鼓励 parakaleō 这个词不太容易翻译。它可以指鼓励，也可以指劝勉，或者兼有两者的意思。作为年轻传道人，你需要了解自己的倾向。你可能更习惯直言真理、劝勉听众，也可能更习惯传递恩典、给人鼓励。 要忠心而有果效地讲道，就必须兼顾恩典与真理，因为耶稣和祂的话语“充充满满地有恩典有真理”（约 1:14）。所以，要有意识地让讲道体现 parakaleō 的双重含义： 在鼓励中劝勉，也在劝勉中鼓励 。 内心的安稳来自救主，不在于讲道表现 有些日子，你觉得自己讲得特别好，很难不欣喜振奋；有些日子，你觉得自己讲砸了，也很容易灰心丧气。讲道结束后，你可能感到不安，也格外脆弱。 有些主日 结束，开车回家路上，你心里空空有种说不出的难受，你会想今天这篇道，到底有没有帮助到会众？朋霍费尔（Dietrich Bonhoeffer）说得对，传道人讲完道，也需要得到牧养。 所以，必须记得回到基督面前，在祂里面得着安稳，不让情绪随着讲道表现起起落落。要把福音讲给 自己 听：神悦纳你，是因为耶稣在十字架上所成就的，而不是因为你在讲台上的表现。你讲道，不是为了让神更爱你，而是因为祂对你的爱已经毫无保留。 身为牧者，你所做的工关乎永恒。地方教会在神对世界的救赎工作中居于核心地位，而传讲神的话语，正是神呼召牧者承担的核心职责。愿神的灵坚固你，使你忠于这份呼召。 谨以主里的爱， 原文刊载于福音联盟英文网站： Letter To a Young Preacher .

articles.title: God Knows Your Name
articles.summary: One particularly catchy book promotion featured the auctioning of the chance for readers to have their name in print. Willing participants could pay to have their names used for a character in a bestselling author’s upcoming novel. The highest bidder in the auction won a chance to select a name to be used in the book.
articles.summary_zh: 一个特别引人注目的书籍促销活动是拍卖读者印刷自己的名字的机会。愿意的参与者可以付费让自己的名字用于畅销书作者即将出版的小说中的角色。拍卖中出价最高的人有机会选择要在书中使用的名称。

articles.title: God’s Portrait of You
articles.summary: The British TV reality show Portrait Artist of the Year pits nine amateur painters against each other in creating portraits of a local celebrity. The images have to be completed in just four hours, which is condensed into the one-hour program. It’s fascinating to watch the cameras capture each artist’s creation slowly emerging from a blank canvas.
articles.summary_zh: 这位英国电视真人秀年度肖像艺术家让九位业余画家互相对立，为当地名人创作肖像。这些图像必须在短短四个小时内完成，并浓缩成一小时的节目。观看相机捕捉每位艺术家从空白画布上慢慢浮现的创作，令人着迷。
